title.narrative: IDP and Famine Response through WASH and Protection in Port Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtOn April 15, 2023, fighting broke out in Khartoum between the SAF and the RSF, quickly spreading to other states and leading to mass displacement. After 17 months, Sudan has become the world’s largest hunger, protection, and displacement crisis with 10.3 million displaced. Red Sea State currently hosts approximately 269,907 IDPs. The influx of IDPs has led to pressures on local infrastructure and the delivery of basic services, like WASH and Protection facilities, aggravating related needs. Water access in Sudan was already precarious before the start of the conflict. At a national level, coverage for drinking water was estimated at 60% as of December 2022. Blue Nile, Gadaref, and Red Sea were the states with the lowest coverage. Without safe drinking water, people have resorted to using water from unsuitable sources. Recently, RSS has seen heavy rains and flooding have continued to cause displacement of people, damaging infrastructure, affecting road access, and heightening the risk of diseases, subsequent flooding are exacerbating the plight of thousands of other vulnerable and acutely food insecure people, compounding their suffering, lack of safety and access to lifesaving assistance and services. Port Sudan currently hosts IDPs in 74 IDP sites through the locality. WASH and Protection needs remain high. This project will respond to the WASH related needs more specifically on water trucking, with a smaller proportion of the project focusing on Protection needs in IDP sites in Port Sudan Locality. The type of activities that were prioritized during the regional consultation meetings in July/August 2024 attended by SHF partners, OCHA, cluster coordinators and focal points as well as the SHF state programs.ltbrgtTherefore, this project will focus on the following outputs and activities: ltbrgtComponent 1: Emergency Water supply accessltbrgtActivity 1: Water trucking to 35 of the 74 IDP camps in Port Sudan (WHH)ltbrgtActivity 2: Provision of Water Storage Facilities (WHH)ltbrgtActivity 3: Rehabilitation of existing water storage facilities ltbrgtActivity 4: Training of Volunteers at IDP Gathering Site on Water ChlorinationltbrgtActivity 5: Water chlorination and monitoring at IDP gathering sitesltbrgtComponent 2: ProtectionltbrgtActivity 1: Establishment of at least one Women and Girls Safe SpaceltbrgtActivity 2: Case management for protection and child protection through mobile teams and Cash for GBV case managementltbrgtActivity 3: PSEA Awareness Raising in Gathering Sites (focus on 2 gathering sites, referrals can cover all gathering sites of the implementing partner)ltbrgtActivity 4: Conduct social norms and awareness on Child Protection issues through interactive theater showsltbrgtWHH aims to address conflict dynamics, minimize negative impacts, and promote peaceful coexistence while delivering essential services. It engages communities, collaborates with local stakeholders, and adapts interventions for sustainability. WHH integrates conflict sensitivity by:ltbrgt1. Context Analysis: Conducting thorough analyses to understand local dynamics, including conflict drivers and power structures, to implement interventions sensitive to conflicts.ltbrgt2. Community Engagement: Consulting local stakeholders, including marginalized and conflict-affected groups, to incorporate their needs and concerns into program design and monitoring.ltbrgt3. Do No Harm Principle: Ensuring equitable resource access and preventing further tensions, while continuously monitoring interventions to adapt based on impact and feedback.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
